The same vectors are run by cargo and by the Node leaf, so there is no second judge table. `resolveHolderLiveness` in the Node leaf becomes an adapter of `judge` (`dead → 'dead'`, `alive | unknown → 'held'`); the one behaviour change is that a record without a pid now reads `held` and a zombie reads `dead`. `pidExists(pid)` (`process.kill(pid, 0)`, `EPERM` counts as existing) is the one helper the cutover phases use in place of every private `isPidAlive` copy, which they delete in the same commit.

**Early ends.** The adapter can end a run before a result: `blocked` (login, folder-trust dialog), `needs-human`, `delivery-unknown` (the brief could not be confirmed and is never resent blind), an agent that finished without leaving. The stop cause stays `cancel` (the closed list of causes is unchanged) and the receipt carries `reason: terminal:<outcome>` (for example `terminal:blocked:trust-dialog`); the settle step turns the screen tail and the reason into the failure the run reports, so a provider limit read from the screen still classifies as `provider-limit`.
| `cleanup-trust` | Node payload | Terminal mode: remove the folder-trust entry the controller wrote for this attempt (only when the controller wrote it) |

- **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself.

The dispatch path has moved twice. First every herdr caller reached herdr only through `fgos internal terminal-control` (`createHerdrClient`, `createBatchTab`, `batchTabFor`, `closeIfEmpty` and the `fgos-lead-*` labels are deleted; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into the round's group). Then the run supervisor took over the round: **the slot key of a run is its attempt id** (`att-...`, the same string the attempt directory and the writer id carry), and its group key is the batch key, else the unit run id. The controller calls `allocate(key = attemptId, groupKey)` once, through the client's per-group queue, before it hands the attempt over; the supervisor then calls `launch`, `send`, `read`, `inspect` and `release` in process by that key, and adopt calls `release` for an attempt whose supervisor is gone. Nothing outside the attempt closes a pane: the confinement reaper and its `terminalKey` home-marker field are deleted, a home belongs to an attempt (run-supervisor spec, section 8). Immediate allocated-slot close and expired-retention close share the foreground safety check: unreadable process information or an unrelated foreground process keeps the pane. A `release(close)` from the supervisor can race an `allocate` that splits from that pane: the core skips a pane that vanished between its liveness check and its geometry read and opens a new tab under the same label when the group has none left, so the race costs a tab, never a wrong close.
